title: The boycott ends
hookLine: some Meccans of conscience tear up the boycott, starting with one man who could no longer eat in peace

cards: A camel is being led through the dark toward the valley where the Prophet's clan is shut in. It is loaded with food.

At the mouth of the valley, Ibn Ishaq tells us, the man leading it takes off its halter, strikes it on the flank, and lets it walk in alone, so nobody can say he broke the agreement. His name is Hisham ibn Amr.
He is not one of the Prophet's followers. He is a Meccan with relatives inside, and the agreement sits badly with him. Today: al-sahifa.

teach.h: HISHAM ASKS: HOW CAN YOU EAT?
teach.b: Ibn Ishaq carries it on from there.
Hisham goes to a man named Zuhayr, whose mother came from the Prophet's own clan, and asks a plain question: how can you eat, and dress, and marry, while your mother's family can't buy or sell?
Zuhayr answers: what can I do? I'm one man. If I had one more with me, I'd act.
You have one, says Hisham. Me. Find us another, says Zuhayr.
And Hisham does. He goes to al-Mut'im ibn Adi, then to Abu al-Bakhtari, then to Zam'a ibn al-Aswad, asking the same question and getting the same answer: not alone.
They meet at night above Mecca and agree on a plan.

teach.h: AT THE KA'BA: TEAR IT UP.
teach.b: In the morning Zuhayr walks around the Ka'ba, turns to the crowd, and says, in effect: people of Mecca, are we going to eat and wear clothes while this clan perishes?
I won't sit down until this unjust, severing document is torn up. Abu Jahl shouts that it will never be torn. Then, one after another, as planned, the others stand and say: tear it.
Al-Mut'im goes to take the document down and finds what we heard yesterday: the insects have eaten it, all but the words, in Your name, O Allah. Notice what did the work. Not an army.
Not a miracle alone. A man with food, a question asked out loud, and a promise not to stand by himself.
The sirah doesn't present these men as believers in the Prophet's message, but as people who decided a rule was wrong and said so, together. It keeps all five of their names.

how: Muslims learn the end of the boycott as part of the Meccan sirah, and the names of the Meccans who worked to end it are kept in Ibn Ishaq's account and retold in sirah study.

the written document, the boycott's terms

games.q: the boycott ends — tap the pairs.
p: sent a camel of food into the valley
went to take the document down
shouted it would never be torn

s: the men who ended the boycott were presented as the Prophet's followers
the sirah presents them as Meccans with family inside who judged it unjust.
Zuhayr first said he couldn't act as one man
Hisham answered: you have one more. me.
the plan was for each man to speak up in turn
they met at night and agreed to back Zuhayr one after another.

games.q: you're Zuhayr. a friend asks how you can eat while your relatives starve. you know you can't change it alone. what do you say?
o: nothing can be done. let it go.
find me one more, and I'll act.
I'll go to the Ka'ba alone right now.
games.why: Ibn Ishaq says Zuhayr asked for one more. Hisham named himself, then went and found others.

practice: Bring to mind one rule, or one habit of a group you're in, that lands hard on someone who can't easily push back, and just see it clearly.
Then do what Hisham did: name one person who might stand with you, and shape one sentence, short and fair, the way Zuhayr spoke at the Ka'ba. Some who pray ask Allah here for the courage to say it.

wordCard.voice: Al-sahifa, the written document. In Ibn Ishaq's telling, a handful of Meccans agree one by one, stand up at the Ka'ba, and it comes down. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the written page or document; the sirah calls the boycott agreement al-sahifa.

carryVoice: Your line: conscience ended it. Five people, and none of them alone. That's day seven hundred forty-seven.

sources.ref: Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah (the annulment of the boycott: Hisham ibn Amr, Zuhayr ibn Abi Umayya, al-Mut'im ibn Adi, Abu al-Bakhtari, Zam'a ibn al-Aswad; the document eaten except 'bismika Allahumma')
